key_insight: The simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner (sPTT) model predicts a purely elastic centre-mode instability in both channel and pipe flows, highlighting the importance of transient rheology.
engineering_relevance: These predictions could help engineers assess viscoelastic flow stability under realistic conditions and discriminate between constitutive models.
method: Numerically analyse linear stability of pressure-driven sPTT channel and pipe flows without inertia.
Explore instability across polymer concentrations and Weissenberg numbers.
Contrast sPTT predictions with models sharing its steady rheology and laminar profiles.
evidence_signal: Numerical results identify instability across a wide range of polymer concentrations and at much lower Weissenberg numbers than previously predicted for purely elastic channel instability.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical linear instability, not experimental validation or proof of subsequent chaotic flow.
paper_title: Purely elastic centre-mode instability in channel and pipe flows of a simplified Phan-Thien-Tanner fluid
